dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between shallow and deep eclipses (depth_ratio 1.9) and the 14.6 d period is half the binary period, the classic sign of an eclipsing binary. With only three highly variable transits and ~1% stellar rotation variability, a planet is not the best explanation.

reasons.why: Strong odd-even depth difference indicates primary and secondary eclipses of an eclipsing binary folded at half the true period, consistent with period_x2 29.2 d. depth_ratio 1.9 with diff_sigma >4 is the classic binary signature.
With only 3 transits share_of_top_3 1.0, depths are not consistent; one or two events drive the 14.31 SNR signal, as also suggested by gaps.near_gap 3 and p_chance 0.01165.
Star shows huge variability (~1% amplitude) on 0.156 d period, star_density_penalty 72.57 and large RUWE 6.305 indicate a spotted/variable binary, not a quiet planet host.
Machine scorer trained on settled candidates rates this as far below the median planet (0.5), supporting a false-positive classification.
